drills.hint: sein is irregular: ich bin, du bist, er ist
haben drops the b: ich habe → du hast, er hat
regular verb gehen; er/sie/es always ends in -t
wir and sie(they) use the full infinitive form -en
stem-changing verb: a→ä in du and er/sie/es
haben + Partizip II; essen is strong: gegessen
Wasser is neuter — das, and all nouns are capitalised
das Brot; rolls are die Brötchen
stronger: danke schön or vielen Dank
die Arbeit = work/job (noun)
colours: rot, blau, grün, gelb
only masculine changes in accusative: der → den
feminine dative: die → der (ich gebe der Frau…)

drills.q: Negate a noun: 'I have ___ time' (no time)?
drills.hint: use kein/keine (not nicht) to negate nouns; Zeit is feminine
nouns ending in -chen are always neuter, das
units first: ein-und-zwanzig (one-and-twenty)

drills.q: How do you say the time 8:30 in German?
drills.hint: halb points to the NEXT hour: halb neun = half to nine

drills.q: How do you ask 'How much does that cost?' in German?
drills.hint: kosten = to cost; das = that

drills.q: How do you say 'I would like...' politely in German?
drills.hint: Konjunktiv II of haben; softer than ich will

drills.q: How do you say 'I don't understand' in German?
drills.hint: nicht comes after the conjugated verb
